newsitem.title: USA: Russia said to free dissident environmentalist.
newsitem.headline: Russia said to free dissident environmentalist.

text.p: Russian authorities have freed Alexander Nikitin, a dissident environmentalist arrested Feb. 6 who was under prosecution for treason, the Union of Councils for Soviet Jews (UCSJ) said in a statement on Saturday.

The group, which coordinated a worldwide campaign to press for Nikitin's release, said it learned of Nikitin's release from his wife, Tatyana Chernova. A news conference was planned in St. Petersburg, Russia on Sunday.

Nikitin has been detained in a St. Petersburg prison since his arrest in February for co-authoring a report commissioned by Norway's Bellona Foundation about nuclear waste disposal in Russia's far north.
Russia accused Nikitin of disclosing state secrets, but UCSJ said the report was based on open sources of non-classified information.

"The UCSJ commends the Russian authorities' decision to free Nikitin, and calls upon them to immediately drop all charges against them," said UCSJ national president Yosef Abramowitz. UCSJ had publicised its campaign on the Internet.
Nikitin had also been identified by Amnesty International as a prisoner of conscience.
